verdict.content_summary: An X thread documenting the AGENTS.md convention as practiced by the Hermes agent: a project-root markdown file that acts as the agent's local source of truth — how the project works, run/test commands, conventions, and no-touch zones — so every session starts from the same foundation instead of rebuilding context from scratch. Replies add three portable mechanisms: a self-briefing bootstrap prompt where the agent reads the README, build files, and recent commits, asks the user what the repo couldn't tell it, and drafts the file itself; a pointer-file interop trick (a CLAUDE.md whose entire content is '@ AGENTS.md'); and hierarchical resolution where the agent walks up to five directory levels and layers per-subdirectory instructions (backend/, frontend/) over parent-level ones. Practitioner discussion of a file convention, not product marketing.

grabs.what: AGENTS.md — a plain markdown file at the project root declaring how the project works, how to run/test it, conventions, and what the agent must never touch
grabs.why: Fits the stack exactly: single static file, no account, no cloud, versioned with the code. Dropping one into each project your local coding/research agents touch means sessions start from structured context instead of re-pasted prose — markdown in, structured behavior out.

grabs.what: Self-briefing bootstrap: the agent reads repo artifacts (README, build files, commit log), interviews the user only for the unstated, then drafts its own context file
grabs.why: A directly portable pipeline pattern — machine ingests structured artifacts, asks the human only about the gap, emits structured markdown. Wire the same prompt shape into your local agents to auto-generate context files for any project or document corpus in your ingest queue.

grabs.what: Pointer-file indirection: thin adapter files whose content is just '@ AGENTS.md' so differently-named agent tools all resolve to one canonical file
grabs.why: Pure small-composable-tool ethos: one source of truth, per-consumer shims. Applies to any multi-agent setup where tools expect differently-named config files — write the adapter, not a second copy that drifts.

grabs.what: Hierarchical context resolution: walk up the directory tree (bounded levels) and layer nearest-scope instructions over parent-scope ones
grabs.why: Port this scoping mechanism to your own pipelines — per-directory instructions for nested projects (backend vs frontend, or per-corpus subdirs in your ingest tree) without a global config blob. Same semantics as .gitignore/.editorconfig, applied to agent behavior.

aspects: Project-local plain-text context file: the agent's operating manual lives as markdown in the repo, versioned alongside the code, not trapped in a chat session
Self-briefing bootstrap: agent ingests existing structured artifacts, interviews the user for what they can't reveal, and emits its own context doc
Pointer-file indirection: '@ AGENTS.md'-style shim files let multiple consumers share one canonical config without duplication
Hierarchical context resolution: bounded walk up the directory tree, nearest-scope instructions layered over parent-scope, .editorconfig-style cascade for agent instructions
adjacency_queries: what other open-source agents treat a plain markdown file in the repo root as the source of truth for project context instead of cloud-synced settings
what CLI tools bootstrap their own configuration by scanning existing project files and asking the user targeted questions about the gaps
what systems resolve configuration hierarchically by walking up the directory tree and merging nearest-scope rules over parent rules like .editorconfig or .gitignore

finds.name: agent-memory
finds.what_it_is: Local, git-native project memory for AI coding agents: plain Markdown committed to the repo is the memory store, with three MCP tools plus a CLI that read/write task state, decisions, conventions, pitfalls, and per-module facts. Branch-aware, secret-safe, explicitly no cloud and no vector DB.
finds.different_angle: Shares the 'markdown in the repo is the agent's source of truth' mechanism, but AGENTS.md is static instructions authored once, while agent-memory is dynamic state the agent reads and writes across sessions — it evolves the convention from a briefing document into working memory with git as the sync layer.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: Matches your stack point-for-point: local-first, no cloud, git as sync, structured MCP/CLI interface (data out, not prose), no account required. It composes with your OpenRouter-routed agents as just another local tool rather than a subscription.

finds.name: agentvault
finds.what_it_is: A local-first knowledge OS where markdown files are the canonical source of truth for notes, decisions, research, tasks, and agent-readable context — with SQLite used purely as a rebuildable index/cache for search, retrieval, and API responses.
finds.different_angle: Same markdown-as-truth mechanism, but from the architecture angle: instead of one convention file, it demonstrates the derived-index pattern — markdown is canonical, the database is disposable state you can rebuild at any time. That split is the portable part.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: This is literally your declared architecture: markdown in, structured queues out, SQLite over managed databases, everything local. Even if you never adopt the tool, the 'markdown truth + rebuildable SQLite index' pattern is a mechanism to lift straight into your ingest pipeline.

finds.name: projectsmd
finds.what_it_is: A MIT-licensed single-file markdown standard for agent-human project collaboration: one .md file captures everything about a project from scoping through execution so agents can resume exactly where work left off, with small Python/Rust tooling around it.
finds.different_angle: Same genre as AGENTS.md — one plain markdown file as a machine-readable contract, convention over tooling — but pointed at state handoff and progress rather than project rules and no-touch zones. It's the 'pick up where you left off' complement to the 'how this repo works' file.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: You favor small single-purpose conventions you can compose, and this is a copyable spec, not a product to buy. Dropping the file format into your markdown-in/structured-out pipeline gives queues resumable project state with zero new dependencies.

finds.name: EditorConfig File Format specification
finds.what_it_is: The canonical spec for EditorConfig: INI files with filepath-glob section scoping, resolved by walking up the directory tree from the file being processed, with a root marker file and nearest-file-wins precedence.
finds.different_angle: This is the long-established prior art for the thread's hierarchical-resolution mechanism: the same walk-up-the-tree, nearest-scope-overrides-parent layering — proven in the editor-settings domain. The glob-section and root-flag constructs are directly reusable designs for per-subdirectory AGENTS.md files.
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: You value mechanisms over products, and this is the smallest complete reference spec for hierarchical file resolution. If you implement 5-level AGENTS.md layering in your own tooling, these are the semantics to copy — the root marker is the detail most reimplementations forget.

finds.name: adobe/himl
finds.what_it_is: Adobe's open-source Apache-2.0 Python library (134★) for hierarchical YAML configuration: merges config files across ordered layers so more-specific scopes override defaults, with value expansion and optional secrets/SSM handling.
finds.different_angle: Attacks the same layered-resolution mechanism as the thread's directory-walking AGENTS.md hierarchy, but from the config-management domain — and as a working merging implementation in code you can read and lift, rather than an agent behavior you prompt for. Its defaults-with-overrides ordering is the generic form of 'subdirectory rules beat parent rules.'
finds.why_relevant_to_profile: Python, self-hostable, no per-seat anything. If your agent tooling needs nearest-scope resolution — per-project and per-subdirectory overrides layered over global defaults — this is runnable code implementing exactly that merge semantics, ready to port.

Skipped coretexthq/coretext (2★, 'License: Other', vague event-sourced framing), Entelligentsia/forge (meta-generator doc page), the DeepWiki shadcn page (third-party docs about an unrelated tool's init flow), and the four duplicate .gitignore doc mirrors (git-scm ×2, dscho, kernel.org — canonical but redundant with the EditorConfig pick).
